title: Pilot bridge and short extension — approval path and next steps
text:
Pilot bridge and short extension — approval path and next steps

["From: Amina Rahman <amina@cobaltai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Becker <tomb@cobaltai.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence — asking for 3-week runway or credit

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the run-through last week. The trial has moved faster than we expected and we're bumping into the planned throughput cap this week. Two asks from our side: 1) a short 3-week bridge to finish our integration tests, or 2) a small credit pool we can draw against while we finish validation (roughly ~120k tokens estimate).

We prefer option 1 (time extension) if it's operationally simpler for you — predictable duration helps our QA schedule. If there is an approval process we should trigger, please let us know the internal steps and any sign-off needed. Tom (procurement) is copied for budget visibility.

Attached is a short usage snapshot for the last two weeks.

Best,
Amina
Head of ML, CobaltAI
--
CobaltAI | amina@cobaltai.com
", "From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amina Rahman <amina@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tomb@cobaltai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence — asking for 3-week runway or credit

Amina — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage snapshot. We can do either but there are differences from a contracting + billing perspective:

- Option A (3-week extension): Operationally straightforward — extend the pilot termination date by 21 days and keep the existing ratecard. Requires manager approval for an out-of-cycle extension.
- Option B (credit pool): Apply one-off platform credits against overage consumption. Faster from approval side, but you'd see split accounting on the invoice.

I can start the approval thread for an extension if you prefer that route. Before I do, a quick question: do you anticipate any additional seat access or throughput bursts during the extension? If so we should include a capped burst allowance.

Copying Rachel (AM) to confirm customer success support during the bridge.

Cheers,
Soojin
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
", "From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Amina Rahman <amina@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tomb@cobaltai.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence — asking for 3-week runway or credit

Amina — happy to support the bridge. For ops: we can allocate a small burst window (up to 2x baseline concurrency) for the 3-week period; we'll throttle automatically beyond that. If you go with credits instead, we recommend the 120k-token estimate as a safety buffer.

If you confirm extension + burst cap, I'll schedule a kickoff with our SRE lead to provision the window and monitor burn.

Also: quick logistical note — legal prefers an addendum for time extensions >14 days; finance needs the expected billing delta for approval.

-rachel
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
", "From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot cadence — asking for 3-week runway or credit

Folks — forwarding CobaltAI's ask. Summary: customer requests a 3-week extension to finish integration tests. Alternate ask: 120k-token credit. We can offer:

1) 21-day extension with a capped burst window (2x concurrency), no change to ratecard. Legal addendum required; low revenue impact.
2) 120k one-off credit applied to June invoice; quicker to approve through finance but complicates invoicing.

Recommended: approve the extension (option 1) as a goodwill/CS play to preserve momentum. Please advise if we need executive sign-off for >21 days or if finance wants a formal approval for credits.

Attaching the usage CSV they sent.

Thanks — Soojin
", "From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Amina Rahman <amina@cobaltai.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence — asking for 3-week runway or credit

Soojin / team / Amina — quick update from finance: we can sign off on a one-time 21-day extension with the capped burst window as long as the extension is explicitly time-boxed and the account owner confirms no additional commercial concessions (no price discount or extra credits). Legal will prepare a very short addendum (1 paragraph) — expect a DocuSign link by EOD Monday.

If CobaltAI prefers the credit route instead, we need a PO or written confirmation and finance will treat credits as contra-revenue applied to the July invoice. That path takes an extra 48-72 hours for internal approvals.

Amina — please confirm which you prefer so we can proceed. If extension: confirm the 21-day window and that you accept the capped burst (2x). We'll aim to have the addendum signed within 72 hours.

Thanks,
David Kim
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
", '(thread note): DocuSign link pending: DocuSign: 0a9b2c3d-pilot-addendum']
